Erica Enders is a six-time Pro Stock World Champion, most recently in 2023. She has 49 national event
wins in Pro Stock. Her most recent victory came at Indianapolis in 2025.

This is her 407th race overall and her 19th appearance at this event. Her first appearance here was
in 2005.

Her best starting position at this event is No. 1, achieved in 2013 and 2022. Her career-best
starting position is No. 1, with 42 such starts. Her average starting position at this event is 4.6,
compared with 5.8 for her career.

Her overall record at this event is 28-13. By round, her record is 14-2 in Round 1, an 87.5% win
rate; 7-7 in Round 2; 4-3 in Round 3; and 3-1 in the final round.

Enders won this race in 2015, defeating Jason Gray; in 2022, defeating Greg Anderson; and in 2023,
defeating Dallas Glenn. She was runner-up here in 2012, losing to Allen Johnson.

She has qualified in the top half of the field in 15 of her 18 appearances here. Her lowest starting
position at this event was No. 15 in 2016. She failed to qualify here in 2006 and 2010.

Her 28 round wins here are the fifth-most she has recorded at any event. Following St. Louis, she
dropped to 10th place in the standing, her lowest position of the year.

Matt Latino has two national event final-round appearances, including one in 2026. His most recent
final was at Charlotte in 2026.

This is his 29th race overall and his second appearance at this event. His first appearance here was
in 2025, when he qualified No. 7.

His career-best starting position is No. 2, achieved at Epping in 2026. His average starting position
for his career is 7.6. His overall record at this event is 0-1.

This is a great side-by-side drag race.

Enders is straight down the groove to go to the number three spot.  Erica Enders' incremental times:
60ft-0.972 sec., 330ft-2.711, 660ft-4.162/169.08 mph, 1,000ft-5.422. 

Latin kept it hooked up to go to the number two spot.  Matt Latino's incremental times: 60ft-0.984
sec., 330ft-2.723, 660ft-4.170/170.02 mph, 1,000ft-5.423.

Jeg Coughlin is a five-time Pro Stock World Champion, most recently in 2013. He has 69 national event
wins in Pro Stock. His most recent victory came at Dallas in 2024.

This is his 514th race overall and his 24th appearance at this event. His first appearance here was
in 1997.

His best starting position at this event is No. 1, achieved five times. His career-best starting
position is No. 1, with 35 such starts. His average starting position at this event is 6.4, compared
with 7.1 for his career.

His overall record at this event is 37-20. By round, his record is 15-7 in Round 1, 13-2 in Round 2,
7-6 in Round 3, and 2-5 in the final round.

Coughlin won this race in 2002, defeating Greg Wilson, and in 2024, defeating Greg Anderson.

He was runner-up here in 2000, losing to Kurt Johnson; in 2003, losing to Greg Anderson; in 2008,
losing to Greg Anderson; in 2018, losing to Tanner Gray; and in 2019, losing to Greg Anderson.

He has qualified in the top half of the field in 13 of his 23 appearances here. His lowest starting
position at this event was No. 16 in 2010. He failed to qualify here in 2001.

His first Pro Stock race was at this event in 1997. His 37 round wins here are tied for the
second-most he has recorded at any event.

Aaron Stanfield has 17 national event wins in Pro Stock, including three victories in 2026. His most
recent win came at St. Louis in 2026.

This is his 130th race overall and his ninth appearance at this event. His first appearance here was
in 2014.

His best starting position at this event is No. 2, achieved in 2022. His career-best starting
position is No. 1, with five such starts. His average starting position at this event is 7.4,
compared with 6.5 for his career.

His overall record at this event is 11-8. By round, his record is 6-2 in Round 1, 4-2 in Round 2, 1-3
in Round 3, and 0-1 in the final round.

Stanfield was runner-up here in 2025, losing to Dallas Glenn. He won this race in Super Stock in 2015
and in Factory Stock in 2020 and 2022.

He has qualified in the top half of the field in five of his eight appearances here. His lowest
starting position at this event was No. 12 in 2014.

Coughlin is straight down the groove to go to the number six spot.

Stanfield launched hard and kept it hooked up to go to the number one spot.  Aaron Stanfield's
incremental times: 60ft-0.969 sec., 330ft-2.698, 660ft-4.148/169.38 mph, 1,000ft-5.408.

Cody Anderson has one national event final-round appearance, most recently at Rockingham in 2026.

This is his 18th race overall and his first appearance at this event. His career-best starting
position is No. 2, achieved at Sonoma in 2026. His average starting position for his career is 7.3.

He has qualified in the top half of the field in 12 of his 17 races this year.

Troy Coughlin Jr. has six national event wins in Pro Stock, including one in 2026. His most recent
victory came at Martin in 2026.

This is his 134th race overall and his seventh appearance at this event. His first appearance here
was in 2020.

His best starting position at this event is No. 2, achieved in 2023. His career-best starting
position is No. 1, achieved four times. His average starting position at this event is 9.0, compared
with 8.8 for his career.

His overall record at this event is 6-6. By round, his record is 3-3 in Round 1, 3-0 in Round 2, 0-3
in Round 3, and 0-0 in the final round.

His best finishes here were semifinal appearances in 2021, 2022, and 2023. His lowest starting
position at this event was No. 15 in 2025. He has qualified in the top half of the field in two of
his six appearances here.

Coughlin set the track's top speed record of 211.09 mph here in 2024 and recorded his career-best
speed of 212.56 mph here in 2023.

Anderson is straight down the groove with a clean pass.

Coughlin launched hard and kept it hooked up to make his quickest and fastest pass this season to go
to the number one spot.  Troy Coughlin Jr.'s incremental times: 60ft-0.973 sec., 330ft-2.701,
660ft-4.149/169.40 mph, 1,000ft-5.407.

Matt Hartford has 11 national event wins in Pro Stock, including three victories in 2026. His most
recent win came at Bristol in 2026.

This is his 230th race overall and his 12th appearance at this event. His first appearance here was
in 2009.

His best starting position at this event is No. 4, achieved in 2020 and 2025. His career-best
starting position is No. 1, with eight such starts. His average starting position at this event is
9.1, compared with 8.3 for his career.

His overall record at this event is 15-10. By round, his record is 9-2 in Round 1, 4-5 in Round 2,
1-3 in Round 3, and 1-0 in the final round.

Hartford won this race in 2020, defeating Greg Anderson. He has qualified in the top half of the
field in six of his 11 appearances here. His lowest starting position at this event was No. 15,
achieved three times.

His 15 round wins here are tied for the most he has recorded at any single event, matching his total
at Indianapolis.

Greg Anderson is a six-time Pro Stock World Champion, most recently in 2024. He has 116 national
event wins, including four victories in 2026. His most recent win came at Brainerd in 2026.

This is his 589th race overall and his 29th appearance at this event. His first appearance here was
in 1998.

His best starting position at this event is No. 1, achieved eight times. His career-best starting
position is No. 1, with 147 such starts. His average starting position at this event is 5.0, compared
with 4.5 for his career.

His overall record at this event is 47-21. By round, his record is 18-9 in Round 1, 13-5 in Round 2,
10-3 in Round 3, and 6-4 in the final round.

Anderson won this race in 2003, defeating Jeg Coughlin; in 2005, defeating Jason Line; in 2009,
defeating Jason Gray; in 2010, defeating Mike Edwards; in 2019, defeating Jeg Coughlin; and in 2021,
defeating Chris McGaha.

He was runner-up here in 2007, losing to Dave Connolly; in 2020, losing to Matt Hartford; in 2022,
losing to Erica Enders; and in 2024, losing to Jeg Coughlin.

He has qualified in the top half of the field in 21 of his 28 appearances here. His lowest starting
position at this event was No. 16 in 2000.

Anderson holds both ends of the track record here, with a performance of 6.457 seconds at 214.59 mph.
He swept this race in 2005 and failed to qualify here in 1998.

Anderson launched hard and kept it hooked up to go to the number one spot.  
Greg Anderson's incremental times: 60ft-0.969 sec., 330ft-2.707, 660ft-4.155/170.28 mph,
1,000ft-5.409. 

Hartford is straight down the groove with a good clean pass.Matt Hartford's incremental times:
60ft-0.987 sec., 330ft-2.720, 660ft-4.166/170.22 mph, 1,000ft-5.419.

Dallas Glenn is the 2025 Pro Stock World Champion and the 2021 Rookie of the Year. He has 25 national
event wins in Pro Stock, including four victories in 2026. His most recent win came at Indianapolis
in 2026.

This is his 109th race overall and his sixth appearance at this event. His first appearance here was
in 2021.

His best starting position at this event is No. 2, achieved in 2021. His career-best starting
position is No. 1, with 14 such starts. His average starting position at this event is 3.8, compared
with 4.9 for his career.

His overall record at this event is 10-3. By round, his record is 4-0 in Round 1, 3-1 in Round 2, 2-1
in Round 3, and 1-1 in the final round.

Glenn won this race in 2025, defeating Aaron Stanfield, and was runner-up here in 2023, losing to
Erica Enders.

He failed to qualify here in 2022, the only DNQ of his career. His lowest starting position at this
event was No. 5 in 2023.

Greg Stanfield has six national event wins in Pro Stock, including two victories in 2026. His most
recent win came at Rockingham in 2026.

This is his 269th race in Pro Stock and his 13th appearance at this event. His first appearance here
was in 2002.

His best starting position at this event is No. 6, achieved in 2010. His career-best starting
position is No. 1, achieved four times. His average starting position at this event is 10.2, compared
with 10.0 for his career.

His overall record at this event is 10-9. By round, his record is 5-5 in Round 1, 3-2 in Round 2, 1-2
in Round 3, and 1-0 in the final round.

Stanfield won this race in 2008, defeating Jeg Coughlin. He has qualified in the top half of the
field in three of his 12 appearances here. His lowest starting position at this event was No. 15 in
2008. He failed to qualify here in 2002 and 2007.

Glenn with a good clean pass to go to the number four spot.

Stanfield kept it hooked up all the way down the track to go to the number one spot.  He makes his
career quickest pass and season fastest.  Greg Stanfield's incremental times: 60ft-0.969 sec.,
330ft-2.698, 660ft-4.146/169.41 mph, 1,000ft-5.403.
